transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood), Liam Chen (NovaCore CTO), Maya Rivera (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (Product)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics \u000B streaming, parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), and retries/robustness. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated; main constraints are latency SLOs and PII handling.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'll do a quick intro then priya will do the live demo, uh feel free to interrupt with questions
[00:14] Liam: thanks jordan, yea we just wanna get a sense of how your hosted API behaves at scale, main thing for us is latency for chat use-cases, and how streaming works with our websocket front-end
[00:30] Priya: perfect, ill share my screen in a sec, quick background - redwood hosted api supports chat and text endpoints, streaming via chunked responses, also built in retry and idempotency helpers, and you can control generation via params like temperature, top_p, stop sequences, and max_tokens
[01:02] Maya: when you say streaming is that SSE or websockets or both? our frontend is websocket based
[01:10] Priya: we support chunked-http streaming (server-sent events) and also websocket proxies via our client libs, there can be slight differences in latency depending on transport but conceptually the token stream is the same. for websocket you can get lower end-to-end latency since you avoid some http overhead
[01:35] Aisha: and how about partial responses - do you get tokens as they're generated or after the model finishes the chunk?
[01:42] Priya: tokens stream as they are emitted by the model, so you can render partial responses progressively. keep in mind there's sometimes micro batching at the runtime level - we try to flush every token or short sequence to minimize perceived latency, but with heavy load aggressive batching might add a few 10s of ms
[02:10] Evan: and that's tunable - we have batching and cache settings per-tenant on dedicated, but on hosted we do dynamic batching with workload-aware heuristics; you can set a latency SLO which will bias away from batching
[02:28] Liam: what's a typical median latency for single-turn chat? our SLA target is sub-300ms for 16-token responses ideally, but we can be flexible
[02:40] Priya: for small outputs (under ~50 tokens) typical end-to-end p50 on our hosted tiers is 120-220ms on models like redwood-v2-small and similar open models, p95 will be higher. i'll caveat - it depends on model selection and prompt length. we'll capture exact numbers in the benchmark run for your payloads
[03:05] Maya: can you explain params briefly? like temperature and top_p - we're trying to understand sampling behavior for deterministic prompts vs creative ones
[03:15] Priya: sure - temperature scales logits randomness, 0.0 is deterministic (greedy), up to 1.0 is more random. top_p is nucleus sampling - choose the smallest token set whose cumulative prob mass exceeds top_p. tldr: temperature+top_p control diversity; for deterministic tasks set temp 0 and lower top_p. also there's repetition_penalty and stop sequences. we recommend explicit stop tokens for structured outputs
[03:50] Jordan: also note we expose max_tokens, token_budget and response_timeouts in the api; you can combine with streaming to cancel earlier if you get the info you need
[04:05] Liam: on retries: if we get transient 5xx from your api, what's your recommended retry strategy? idempotency keys? backoff?
[04:15] Priya: yes use idempotency keys for non-streamed requests; for streaming we recommend a short exponential backoff + jitter and resume using conversation state. we also return semantically useful retryable error codes. our client SDK includes a retry helper that respects token usage and avoids duplicate billing in most cases
[04:45] Aisha: duplicate billing - how does that work with retries on generation? if we retry, do we get charged twice?
[04:52] Evan: good q - we try to avoid double billing by correlating idempotency keys and using a retry cache for a short window; streaming retries can be trickier but our SDK uses resume tokens where possible so you don't re-run the whole decode. we'll share the doc that details billing semantics
[05:10] Priya: alright demo time - i'm going to show a quick curl to the chat endpoint then switch to the console which shows streaming and params controls
[05:22] [screen share starts]
[05:30] Priya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following: The sales team needs to..."}],"max_tokens":60,"temperature":0.2}'
[06:01] Priya: that returns a streamed response chunks look like this: {"delta":{"content":"..."}} and you get incremental content. on the console we also show token-level timing to help debug latency hot spots
[06:25] Maya: that console tracing looks useful - can we get per-request traces to our datadog?
[06:32] Priya: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward spans/logs to datadog or new relic; there's a tracing header you can set to get end-to-end traces. we also provide per-route dashboards in the console
[06:50] Liam: security - we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. also data residency in eu-west for some of our customers. do you support that on hosted?
[07:05] Jordan: hosted has region controls - europe regions available and data processed there when you pick region. SOC 2 Type II is completed, we have SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and KMS integrations for private deployments; hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and in-transit and we provide audit logs via the console with retention options as an add-on
[07:38] Aisha: is there an option to bring your own key to hosted? BYOK?
[07:44] Evan: hosted supports cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), customers can bring keys in some enterprise tiers; for strict BYOK/HSM you might look at private deployment where you manage keys and the control plane sits in your VPC
[08:05] Priya: switching back - now i'll demo parameter tuning: i have three examples: deterministic summarization (temp 0), creative marketing copy (temp 0.9), and constrained json output (stop sequences + max_tokens).
[08:28] [demo: three side-by-side requests run, console shows token stream and latency rows]
[08:40] Priya: you can see creative example is longer and more diverse; deterministic is compact. for structured outputs we also recommend using system messages to set schema, and leverage our structured output validators post-response
[09:00] Liam: do you have built-in validators? or is that in optimize?
[09:05] Priya: basic schema checks are in the api tooling, more advanced quality monitoring and regression alerts are part of Redwood Optimize which can run prompt-based evals over time and surface quality regressions tied to model changes
[09:25] Maya: about rate limits - what are default rps limits and how do you handle bursts?
[09:32] Jordan: default rate limits depend on account tier; hosted has soft burst support and token-based quotas. for predictable throughput we offer Dedicated where you get reserved GPU capacity. for hosted you can request higher limits; we also have token throttling policies and graceful fallback to smaller model variants when capacity constrained
[10:00] Aisha: fallback how deterministic is it? if you fallback to a smaller model could that change output semantics and break our product?
[10:09] Priya: yes it could; fallback is configured as a policy - by default we notify via header when fallback happens and you can pin routes to specific model versions for strict determinism. recommended for production-critical flows is either pinning or Dedicated capacity
[10:28] Liam: ok we want a pilot on hosted to start, but we may test Dedicated later. timeline wise we're aiming to ship a beta in q3. interested in trial keys and a short PoC to validate latency and costs
[10:45] Jordan: great - we'll provision trial keys and run an initial benchmark. priya can run the latency/cost bench on your sample prompts.
[11:00] [brief side conversation about sampling formats and retry headers - some cross talk]
[11:30] Priya: quick note on retries for streaming - if a stream is interrupted you can use a resume token or just fetch the last assistant message and re-request the continuation; our SDK exposes helpers for common frameworks
[12:02] Maya: are there examples for node/react? our frontend is react with websockets
[12:10] Priya: yes our JS SDK includes websocket helpers and react hooks; i'll share code snippets after the call
[12:28] Aisha: curious about cost - what are typical per-1k-token costs for hosted? and any volume discounts?
[12:36] Jordan: pricing varies by model family - small models are cheaper per token; we do volume tiers and committed usage discounts for Dedicated. i'll include a pricing matrix in the follow-up email.
[12:50] Liam: also need to confirm data retention policy for hosted and logs - we need logs deleted after 90 days and some PII redaction
[13:00] Evan: hosted includes configurable retention windows; PII redaction is available via integration or pre-processing; for strict requirements we recommend private deployment where you control data retention fully
[13:16] [demo wraps up, screen share stops]
[13:25] Priya: ok i'm going to show the console route config briefly - here you can pin models, set max tokens, default temp, and enable streaming by default; also set response timeouts and set the retry policy per-route
[13:50] Maya: can we set different configs per-environment (prod/staging)?
[13:56] Priya: yes environments and multiple api keys with scoped roles, and RBAC in the console - you can make staging keys less permissive and route traffic differently
[14:12] Liam: what's the onboarding like for enterprise - docs, benchmarks, support?
[14:20] Jordan: self-serve docs + SDKs, we'll run an onboarding workshop for the pilot, provide a bench spreadsheet and run the benchmark together. for enterprise there's a solutions engineering engagement and SLA options
[14:40] Aisha: ok sounds good. final question: for streaming we saw quite low latency - is there jitter during peak times?
[14:50] Priya: there can be more jitter at p95 during peak but p50 remains stable; levers to control are model selection, setting a latency SLO, and enabling cache for common prefixes which reduces variability
[15:10] Jordan: quick recap & next steps - we'll: 1) send pricing + trial credentials, 2) priya will run a custom bench using your prompts, 3) lia m will share sample prompts and traffic profile, 4) schedule deep-dive on private options if needed
[15:30] Liam: yep thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll get the prompts over.
[15:40] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up by monday with the deck and keys

Notes/Artifacts shared: console screenshot (link: https://redwood.ai/share/console-demo-20260605), benchmark template (link: https://redwood.ai/bench/novacore-template), security whitepaper (link: https://redwood.ai/security/whitepaper.pdf)
